players.product: antibody discovery and multispecific T-cell engager platform

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Carl Hansen on ABCL635, AbCellera's first-in-class anti-NK3R antibody for vasomotor symptoms (menopause, and induced menopause with endocrine therapy in breast and prostate cancer), which entered the clinic at the start of the year: the phase II (a single 600-milligram injection) top-line 4-week data showed, in cross-trial comparisons he said should be taken 'with a grain of salt', efficacy roughly twice that of the two approved small molecules (Bayer's Lynkuet and Astellas' VEOZAH) on hot-flash frequency and '4 or 5 times' on the severity score; a 5.1 reduction in daily events against an approval bar of at least two; 37% of patients going from around 10 events per day to zero and about 24% with a zero severity score; no evidence of elevated liver enzymes; 80% of patients saying they felt much better or better; and a sleep benefit at least on par with Lynkuet. No degradation was seen at four weeks, and the 600-milligram dose simulates the steady state of a once-monthly dose of 300 milligrams, so the once-a-month dosing target is met.
quarterly_data.figure: efficacy roughly twice the small molecules on frequency, 4 or 5 times on severity; 5.1 reduction; 37% to zero events; about 24% zero severity score; 80% felt better

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Carl Hansen on ABCL635 next steps: 12-week data and the 12-week open-label extension should be in hand by the end of the year; AbCellera will then engage the FDA, Health Canada, EMA and maybe Australia and try to start a phase III trial in the back half of next year. ABCL635 has been admitted to the FDA Model-Informed Drug Development Program, whose modeling will inform dose and interval; he currently thinks roughly 1,500 patients would be appropriate for the safety database, with co-primary endpoints of frequency and severity reduction, and AbCellera may include more than one dose. Before the registrational study it will initiate two phase II trials, breast cancer probably first and then prostate cancer. The study is probably 2 and a half years and 'A launch around 2030 would be about right'; he called these impressions, not plans, until AbCellera talks with regulators.
quarterly_data.figure: 12-week data by end of year; phase III start back half of next year; roughly 1,500 patients; launch around 2030

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Carl Hansen on commercialization: AbCellera is 'not commercial ready' and does not need to be yet; whether it commercializes ABCL635 itself is 'not yet decided'. The vision is a multi-product commercial company that competes on global markets, possibly using direct pay, direct-to-consumer and technology-forward distribution rather than '1,500 sales reps', while 'the right commercial alliance with the right partner under the right terms could also be a game changer'; AbCellera is entertaining conversations but making sure it is fully capitalized to go on its own, his favorite scenario. He sees non-hormonal VMS as 'a multi-billion dollar opportunity' given the robust growth of the two small molecules, and ABCL635 as a potential 'multi-blockbuster opportunity' that could be 'the dominant product for non-hormonal treatment of menopause symptoms' if the data translate to phase III.

CEO Carl Hansen on the pipeline: ABCL688 and ABCL386 are on track to be in the clinic next year, there are two more programs in the pipe, and AbCellera expects another development candidate this year; a longer-half-life ABCL635 follow-on is already in IND-enabling studies. After this year AbCellera may stop announcing development candidates until they reach the clinic, for competitive reasons. AbCellera officially transitioned to building its own assets in September 2023, and he said the platform and the drugs it will make are the most valuable thing about the company going forward.
quarterly_data.figure: ABCL688 and ABCL386 in the clinic next year; another development candidate expected this year
